outcome: maternal complications (LSCS, PPH, sepsis, instrumental delivery)
perinatal morbidity (acute foetal distress, meconium stained liquor, asphyxia, NICU admission)
cohort: 200 pregnant patients from an antenatal ward and labour room, divided into a control group (gestational age 37-40 weeks) and a study group (gestational age >40 weeks).
finding: Postdated pregnancies (gestational age >40 weeks) were associated with a significantly higher incidence of maternal complications, perinatal morbidity (asphyxia, NICU admission), and perinatal mortality (intrauterine deaths) compared to term pregnancies.
mod_finding: Postdated pregnancies had a higher rate of LSCS (30% vs 15%) and instrumental deliveries (13% vs 7%) compared to term pregnancies.
